source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
ORD1 publishes 147.6 MW of combined utility power serving 237,000 square feet of technical space. The split between utility feed and IT load is not published, so a clean translation requires an assumption: if IT load runs at roughly 60 percent of utility draw, that implies about 88 MW of IT capacity, and at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that is roughly 2,200 racks, enough for several thousand GPU-class accelerators. Those figures are a derived estimate, not an operator claim.

The five certifications tell a precise story about qualified workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the facility for audited financial and operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data. ISO 27001 qualifies it for internationally benchmarked information security management. NIST 800-53 qualifies it for federal and regulated-sector workloads where that control framework is required.

Illinois has 44 mapped facilities in this site's index, but only 6 of those publish a megawatt figure, totaling 236 MW across those six. ORD1's 147.6 MW is larger than that six-facility total, which means it ranks seventh by published MW in the state only because at least six other sites have published larger or equal figures. The gap between 44 mapped facilities and 6 with published capacity means the true Illinois picture is substantially undercounted, and ORD1's relative position could shift as more operators publish specs.
